summary.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
summary.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,650 crores, up 28% YoY; accounted for about 63% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Non-housing / LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 958 crores, up 32% YoY; about 37% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Self-employed (SENP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 44% YoY; current NPA around 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% in salaried, per management.

segments.name: Karnataka / Telangana
segments.commentary: All six zones grew; Karnataka grew 18% YoY (lowest zone), Telangana slightly higher. IT-sector exposure about 6% of customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.
Bank borrowing rates for new loans now 7.25-7.5% vs about 6.95% last year; existing loans unchanged.
Special-rate threshold raised from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh loans, to offset higher incremental borrowing costs.
Customer pricing range about 8.4% (best, salaried, CIBIL above 725, INR 25 lakh+) to about 12.5% (non-salaried, non-housing, S3); blended yield 9.81%.
Competition: LIC and Bajaj Housing are the main rivals in branches; Bajaj growing around 25-30% per analyst comment, with its technology edge cited.
Best rate gap to banks widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps after repo cuts; management says it cannot close the gap cheaply.
82% of loans now have CIBIL score above 700 (vs about 75% earlier); 80% of business sourced via DSA.
